sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioners have been falsely implicated in the present case.

It was contended that as per the prosecution, the petitioner Virma Ram appeared in the competitive examination conducted by the RPSC in the year 2017-18 for the post of Headmaster in place of petitioner Val Singh Ganawa.
Learned counsel further contended that investigation against the petitioners has already been completed and challan has been filed.

Lastly, learned counsel submitted that the petitioners are in judicial custody and the trial of the case will take sufficiently long time, therefore, the benefit of bail may be granted to the accused-petitioners.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor has vehemently opposed the bail applications.

Having considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case, this Court prima facie finds that investigation against the petitioners has already been completed; the petitioners are in judicial custody and the prosecution has not shown any apprehension of the petitioners influencing the prosecution witnesses or fleeing away from justice in case they are enlarged on bail.
Thus, without expressing any opinion on merits/demerits of the case, this Court is of the opinion that the bail applications filed by the petitioners deserve to be accepted.
Consequently, these bail applications under Section 483 of BNSS (439 Cr.P.C.) are allowed.

It is ordered that the accused- petitioners (1) Val Singh Ganawa S/o Shri Dhulji Ganawa and [2024:RJ-JD:45752] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-12229/2024] (2) Virmaram S/o Shri Gangaram arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.190/2024 registered at Police Station Kushalgarh, District Banswara,
shall be released on bail, if not wanted in any other case, provided each of them furnishes a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each, to the satisfaction of learned trial court,
for their appearance before that court on each & every date of hearing and whenever called upon to do so till completion of the trial.
A copy of this order be placed in each file.
